Assuming you have a table named "orders" with columns "customer_id", "order_date" and "order_count", the SQL query would look like this:

```sql
SELECT customer_id
FROM orders
WHERE order_date >= DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE, INTERVAL 90 DAY)
GROUP BY customer_id
HAVING COUNT(order_id) > 3;
```

This query first filters the orders to only include those placed in the last 90 days. It then groups the remaining orders by customer_id. The HAVING clause is used to filter these groups to only include those where the count of orders is greater than 3.
